description:
Approved by the user 2026-11-17 (relayed verbatim by JSON: "B,C,D proceed."). Probe evidence: JSON session scratchpad jsonenc/.

Defect: acc <> "ab" allocates a 16 B bitstring for the literal on every append (a literal <= 64 bytes goes through fz_alloc_bitstring_const). About 20 per object in the docs encode: ~122k bitstrings, 1.95 MB per encode.

Relation: fz-sc8.236 (user-combined 2026-11-17) emits a short string literal as a read-only static object instead of fz_alloc_bitstring_const, which removes this allocation for every literal use, appends included. Re-measure on .236 first; what remains here is only copying the literal's bytes straight into the append without materialising an operand. One mechanism, not two.

Done when: a fixture shows 0 literal bitstrings per append on all three paths.

comments.text: Measured on #740 (8d32c0271) vs develop (JSON, 2026-11-18): literal appends make 0 literal bitstrings on all three paths; acc <> "true" 625 -> 459 instr per append; docs encode bitstrings 170,847 -> 24,445. The work is done by fz-sc8.236. Remaining: the proof fixture (literal vs non-literal control, equal alloc deltas), landed as this ticket's commit after #740 merges; then close.

title: Appending a literal copies its bytes; no bitstring is made for it
